introHeading: The mirror booth, built for Brooklyn's rooms
introParas: Our magic mirror is the booth that put this whole category on the map, and in Brooklyn it is still the one couples and event planners ask for by name. Behind the gold frame sits a Canon DSLR and a studio ring light, so the photos look shot in a studio rather than snapped on a phone in a dark tent. The touchscreen itself does the heavy lifting — animated prompts, a voice walking guests through the pose, and a fingertip signature guests can leave right on their print.

It travels well into the venues we see most in this borough: up the narrow stairwell of a Park Slope brownstone, through a Bushwick warehouse's freight elevator, onto a Williamsburg rooftop with the skyline lit up behind the backdrop. Because it reads at full height, whole wedding parties can pile in at once instead of squeezing three people into a frame, and it is the rare booth that grandparents use as happily as the dance floor crowd — which is why it is still our most-booked rental for Brooklyn weddings, Sweet Sixteens and bar and bat mitzvahs, alongside the corporate holiday parties that fill lofts in Downtown Brooklyn and Greenpoint.

Setup takes about 20 minutes and we arrive a full hour ahead of your start time, so it is tested and quiet before your first guest walks in. The booth wants a 10ft x 10ft footprint with room for a backdrop and props table, though we can compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for a tighter loft or brownstone parlor floor, and all it needs is a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet. There is no travel fee anywhere in Brooklyn, whether your venue sits in Bay Ridge or Crown Heights — we quote everything from your venue ZIP before you book.

faqHeading: Mirror Photo Booth in Brooklyn — FAQ

faqs.q: Is the mirror booth good for a wedding in a Park Slope brownstone?
faqs.a: Yes — we compress the footprint to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for a tighter brownstone parlor floor, and our attendant carries the road cases up narrow stairs as part of the setup. The full-length mirror still gives guests the same touchscreen experience even in the smaller footprint.

faqs.q: Can the mirror booth get through a Bushwick warehouse's freight elevator?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Bushwick and other converted-warehouse venues are some of the most common setups we run in Brooklyn, and we plan the load-in around freight elevator size and loading dock access before we ever arrive. Tell us your venue and we will confirm exactly how the booth gets in.

faqs.q: Do you charge extra to bring the mirror booth to a Williamsburg rooftop?
faqs.a: No travel fee anywhere in Brooklyn, rooftops included. We do ask about outdoor power access and weather protection ahead of time, since a rooftop setup needs a dry, level spot and a standard outlet within 15 feet of the booth.

faqs.q: Can guests sign or write on their photo at the mirror booth?
faqs.a: Yes. The touchscreen supports on-screen signatures and drawings, so guests can leave a message right on their print — a favorite feature at Brooklyn weddings where the couple keeps every strip in a guest book afterward.

faqs.q: How much space does the mirror booth need?
faqs.a: The optimal footprint is 10ft x 10ft, which leaves room for the backdrop, props table and a red carpet if you want one. We can compress to a minimum of 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for a tighter Brooklyn loft or brownstone floor, and we need one standard 110V outlet within 15 feet.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with a Brooklyn mirror booth rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for the full length of your Brooklyn rental — setup, keeping the prop table organized, helping guests use the touchscreen, and packing down at the end of the night.

faqs.q: How long does setup take, and can you arrive early for a Brooklyn event?
faqs.a: Setup takes about 20 minutes once we are in the room, and we arrive a full hour before your scheduled start time so everything is tested and quiet before guests arrive. If your Brooklyn venue needs us on site earlier than that, idle time runs $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance and can you provide a COI for a Brooklyn venue?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy. If your Brooklyn venue needs a certificate of insurance naming them as additionally insured, reply to your booking confirmation with their contact email and we will send it over.
